tldr: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 3.8 Live with an Extended Thinking mode on September 15, adding real-time reasoning to the 3.8 line's voice and video agent capabilities. It followed up on September 23 with two new Flash-tier text-to-speech models carrying a 2,000+ voice library.
whats_new: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar reached general availability in Gemini Enterprise on September 24, a week after the Live and Extended Thinking launch.
why_it_matters: GA status on Live Avatar plus the Flash-tier TTS pair lets agent builders wire reasoning, speech, and an avatar front-end into one voice agent on Gemini without stitching in a separate TTS or avatar vendor.

status.detail: Live with Live Avatar exited preview into general availability in Gemini Enterprise; the TTS model pair has been in general release since Sep 23.

beats.headline: Gemini 3.8 Live ships with an Extended Thinking mode
Two new Gemini 3.8 TTS models ship with 2,000+ voices
Developers build a TTS playground and a voice-direction guide
Live with Live Avatar goes GA in Gemini Enterprise

open_questions: Do the new TTS models support streaming synthesis for real-time voice agents, or batch-only output?
How does gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts's latency and per-character cost compare to competing low-latency TTS APIs?
Is Live Avatar available outside the Gemini Enterprise tier, or gated behind that tier's pricing?
take_for_builders: Building a voice agent on Gemini: try gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts on latency-sensitive paths, use Willison's playground or philschmid's guide to audition voices, and check whether your Gemini Enterprise tier already includes GA Live Avatar before evaluating a third-party avatar vendor.
